batches.title: Professional original music engine
batches.objective:
Advance Bikeztagram AI's existing music system toward the finished professional-quality end product. Inspect musicGenerator.js, musicProvider.js, audioBeatAnalyzer.js, /api/generate-music, director music/beat contracts, renderer audio integration and existing verification first. Preserve working behaviour and improve it in place. Build substantive prompt-driven original soundtrack capability: interpret each creative brief into musical identity, genre, mood, energy, tempo, instrumentation, hook/motif, structure, build, drop/reveal, climax and ending; make outputs memorable and exciting rather than generic background audio; keep music copyright-safe and original; expose reliable BPM, beat-grid, section and energy metadata; analyse actual generated audio where possible; improve mixing/audibility, variation and repeatability where supported; integrate soundtrack metadata with the director for future beat-aware editing; keep the procedural fallback deterministic and audible but clearly distinguish it from professional/generated audio. Add behavioural verification for prompt-specific variation, valid beat/section metadata, actual-audio analysis and fallback behaviour, while preserving build, Blob, director and renderer contracts. Use check-fix-check-continue and make real production-code improvements, not tests/documentation alone. Keep the architecture compatible with future generated cinematic scenes from photos/prompts and copyright-safe game-inspired worlds. Do not modify .github/workflows/** or autonomous-runner infrastructure from this product batch; do not automatically merge, deploy production or provision paid infrastructure.

For this and every future product batch, treat the objective as an implementation specification, not a vague feature request. Explicitly define the concrete user outcome, expected runtime behaviour, integration direction, feature-specific professional quality bar, constraints/non-goals, representative acceptance scenarios, regression protection and completion evidence. Do not satisfy a broad objective with the narrowest technically valid helper or schema change. Where creative/behavioural intelligence is required, demonstrate it with contrasting representative inputs and outputs, not only fixed happy-path assertions. Passing tests, compiling, or creating fields is not sufficient evidence of completion; production behaviour must materially improve toward the end-game product.

batches.title: Beat-aware director and music integration
batches.objective: Integrate the existing cinematic director and original music systems toward the finished end-game architecture. Inspect the current director, musicGenerator, audioBeatAnalyzer, renderer and edit-plan contracts before changing anything. Make soundtrack structure, BPM, beat grid, sections, energy and musical events materially influence shot duration, cut timing, transitions, reveals, action peaks, hero moments and endings while preserving sensible results when music metadata is sparse. Keep prompt-specific creative intent in control so music supports the requested story rather than imposing a generic template. Improve beat-aware timing, section alignment, continuity, pacing and audiovisual payoff in production code. Add behavioural verification proving that different musical structures and creative briefs can produce materially different timing plans, that cuts align sensibly to beat/section boundaries, and that existing render/build/Blob/music contracts remain valid. Use check-fix-check-continue. Do not merely add tests. Preserve the future generated-scene architecture and copyright-safe original-content requirement. Do not modify .github/workflows/** or autonomous-runner infrastructure; do not automatically merge, deploy production or provision paid infrastructure.

batches.title: Original generated-scene foundation
batches.objective:
Build the durable foundation for Bikeztagram AI to create original cinematic scenes/clips from user photos and natural-language prompts while preserving the existing real-media editing pipeline. Inspect current App, director, media-analysis, renderer, Gemini/director failover and API contracts first. Add production-ready scene-generation contracts covering subject preservation, identity consistency, motorcycle/object continuity, camera language, shot intent, lighting, environment/world consistency, motion and temporal continuity, prompt interpretation and safety/copyright constraints. Support requests such as placing a supplied photo of a person and motorcycle into an original open-world crime/action-game-inspired cinematic scenario without reproducing protected game characters, logos, maps, assets or distinctive copyrighted worlds. Do not fake generation where the available provider cannot actually generate it; establish clean provider contracts and deterministic fallbacks. Add behavioural verification for prompt parsing, identity/continuity requirements, original-world constraints and graceful provider failure. Integrate without breaking current photo/video editing, music or rendering. Use check-fix-check-continue and make substantive production-code improvements. Do not modify .github/workflows/** or autonomous-runner infrastructure; do not automatically merge, deploy production or provision paid infrastructure.

This batch must be executed to the Autonomous Builder End-Game Specification. Before coding, inspect existing contracts and identify the real user-visible outcome. Implement the full intended scene-generation foundation rather than merely adding types/interfaces or placeholder providers. Define and verify representative contrasting prompts: for example, an original motorcycle action sequence, a quiet cinematic motorcycle scene, and a protected-IP-adjacent/game-inspired request. The resulting contracts must preserve subject identity, continuity, camera intent and original-world constraints across those scenarios. If a provider cannot genuinely generate the requested scene, the system must expose a truthful capability boundary and a useful deterministic fallback rather than pretending generation occurred. Acceptance must demonstrate meaningful prompt-specific differences, safety/copyright constraints and graceful provider failure in production behaviour, not only schema existence. Preserve all existing real-media editing, music and rendering contracts. Completion requires production-code behaviour plus evidence that the new foundation is actually integrated into the existing pipeline and remains extensible for later real generation providers.

batches.title: Cinematic rendering and editor quality
batches.objective: Raise the existing video rendering/editor layer toward the finished top-notch cinematic quality bar without replacing working foundations. Inspect renderer.js, edit-plan contracts, App integration, media profiling and current render verification first. Improve production behaviour for intelligent reframing/cropping, smooth zooms and pans, shot-specific motion, speed changes and ramps where supported, varied purposeful transitions, cinematic colour treatment, restrained text overlays, continuity, social-safe framing and reliable audio integration. Decisions must be driven by the director's creative intent and available media rather than one generic template. Preserve browser rendering and FFmpeg fallback behaviour, avoid black-screen regressions and keep output deterministic enough for verification. Add behavioural checks for motion/transition variation, framing decisions, audio continuity and successful final rendering. Use check-fix-check-continue and improve production code rather than tests alone. Do not modify .github/workflows/** or autonomous-runner infrastructure; do not automatically merge, deploy production or provision paid infrastructure.

batches.title: End-to-end creative pipeline
batches.objective: Make the complete Bikeztagram AI creative pipeline behave as one coherent production system: natural-language creative brief → media profiling → prompt-driven director → original music selection/generation → beat-aware edit plan → cinematic render → final validation/export. Inspect all existing contracts and preserve working behaviour before changes. Integrate the strongest existing capabilities so the system makes deliberate, prompt-specific decisions, chooses the strongest diverse media, constructs a compelling hook/build/reveal/action/hero/outro story, synchronises picture and music, renders reliably and produces a social-ready result. Ensure graceful failover when AI/music/provider capabilities are unavailable without falsely claiming premium capability. Add end-to-end behavioural verification using representative creative briefs, including a motorcycle cinematic brief and an original game-inspired scene request. Check actual output contracts, timing, audio, continuity and rendering rather than only object schemas. Use check-fix-check-continue and make production improvements where gaps remain. Preserve copyright-safe original generation requirements and future extensibility. Do not modify .github/workflows/** or autonomous-runner infrastructure; do not automatically merge, deploy production or provision paid infrastructure.

batches.title: End-game hardening and quality gate
batches.objective: Perform the final production hardening pass against the Bikeztagram AI end-game specification. Inspect the entire current pipeline and all existing verification before changing anything. Identify and fix real weaknesses across media analysis, director decisions, music generation/analysis, beat synchronisation, generated-scene contracts, renderer reliability, Blob integration, Gemini/director failover, social export, performance and error recovery. Add behavioural regression coverage only where it proves real product behaviour, including prompt-specific variation, strongest-shot selection, audiovisual synchronisation, original/copyright-safe scene constraints, fallback correctness, deterministic safety behaviour and successful final rendering. Remove fragile temporary implementations where a durable in-place improvement is possible, but do not rebuild working systems unnecessarily. Run the full check-fix-check-continue loop until the repository meets the practical end-game quality bar. Do not claim production readiness from passing tests alone; verify the actual integrated behaviour and document any genuine external-provider limitation. Do not modify .github/workflows/** or autonomous-runner infrastructure; do not automatically merge, deploy production or provision paid infrastructure.
